LESSON: LENGTH

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Measurement
Topic 2.1: Length
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Length, part of Measurement in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How do you measure distance? 2. Why do you measure distance?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Discuss in purposive groups/pairs the kilometre as a unit of measuring length real life. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative and augmentative modes of communication (AAC) or use residual speech or be lip-read by peers, learner support assistance or teacher to discuss unit of measuring length.

2. Team up with peers to estimate distance in kilometres. More time could be allowed for learners with manipulation difficulties to perform the task. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Discuss in purposive groups/pairs the kilometre as a unit of measuring length real life. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative and augmentative modes of communication (AAC) or use residual speech or be lip-read by peers, learner support assistance or teacher to discuss unit of measuring length.
2. Team up with peers to estimate distance in kilometres. More time could be allowed for learners with manipulation difficulties to perform the task. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Length together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
● Integrity: as the learner shows integrity as they measure and record estimated distances practically using ropes and other

learning materials.

● Respect: as the learner shows respect as they take turn in measuring distance in kilometres practically using ropes.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Safety: as the learner observes safety precautions while handling measuring instruments to enhance safety.

Link to other subjects:

The learner is able to link measurement of length to construction a food preservation equipment in Agriculture and Nutrition.
